transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net network infrastructure technical operations, my name is Toby. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Toby, my name is Kieran Walsh. I run a Synology NAS storage server for my architectural firm, but ever since my broadband upgraded to your Fibre 500 package, external DDNS remote access has completely stopped working because my WAN IP is trapped behind Carrier-Grade NAT!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good afternoon Kieran. I can inspect your broadband WAN routing and public IP allocation parameters. Before we access your gateway telemetry, could you confirm your full postal address and your account security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 58 Park Avenue, Manchester, M14 5JH, and my security PIN is 8841. My router model is the Hub 5 with WAN IP starting with one hundred dot sixty-four.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Kieran, that confirms your account details. What specific error is reported by the Synology DDNS service?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The Synology DiskStation manager displays 'External IP 100.64.182.49 does not match public DNS resolution. Port forwarding unreachable.' because having a reliable home broadband connection is absolutely essential for our daily household work.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So what has occurred is that following your optical line upgrade, your Hub 5 was provisioned with a shared RFC 6598 Carrier-Grade NAT address in the 100.64 block, preventing inbound port forwarding to your local Synology NAS server, is that right in accordance with our standard telecommunications network diagnostic procedures.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that is exactly what happened! I have three freelance draughtsmen working remotely across the UK who cannot access our thirty-gigabyte CAD blueprints! We have planning permission submissions due by midnight, and our external workflow is completely crippled! I demand that S-Net assign a dedicated permanent static IPv4 address to my connection right now at zero charge so I really appreciate you taking the time to look into these technical details with me today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Bear with me for a couple of minutes while I check our regional CGNAT gateway pools and subscriber IP assignment profiles in the Manchester aggregation core across all your connected household devices including laptops, mobile phones, and streaming hardware.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for waiting, Kieran. The Manchester broadband network gateway confirms your dynamic session is routed through a CGNAT carrier translation pool to maintain optimal throughput and low latency across the regional distribution network.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand how critical and urgent it is to maintain seamless remote file access for your architectural draughtsmen when major planning deadlines are pending tonight, Kieran. However, because our residential broadband service tier utilizes CGNAT pooling to conserve global IPv4 space, our service terms do not permit issuing permanent static IP addresses on standard consumer subscriptions; what I can do right now is assign an immediate CGNAT opt-out profile to your account, giving your Hub 5 a dedicated public dynamic IPv4 address from our unrestricted pool, and enable automated UPnP port mapping to ensure your S-Net service operates reliably without unexpected dropped packets or connection faults.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: A dedicated public dynamic IPv4 address will work completely fine with my Synology DDNS! As long as inbound port forwarding is unrestricted, DDNS will update automatically because having a reliable home broadband connection is absolutely essential for our daily household work.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am applying the CGNAT Opt-Out Public IP profile to your broadband circuit on our RADIUS provisioning server right now so that your account records and provisioning parameters remain completely up to date.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How do we bind the new public IP to my Hub 5 router so I really appreciate you taking the time to look into these technical details with me today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will send a remote port bounce command to re-negotiate your PPPoE WAN session to maintain optimal throughput and low latency across the regional distribution network.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The router internet light just turned amber for a moment...

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The WAN interface is requesting a fresh IP lease from our public carrier pool.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The light is back to solid white! Let me check the Hub 5 WAN status page... It has been assigned IP address 82.132.214.88! That is a genuine public IP address!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: 82.132.214.88 is a fully routable public IPv4 address with completely unrestricted inbound port forwarding.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me check the Synology DiskStation DDNS status page right now... Clicking 'Update Now'...

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The Synology client should query public DNS and bind port five thousand and one.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The Synology screen says 'Status: Normal'! External IP matched successfully! Let me test remote access from my mobile phone on 5G...

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously Carrier-Grade NAT is implemented across residential access networks in accordance with Ofcom IPv4 exhaustion guidelines.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am connecting via 5G... Tapped our firm's DDNS URL... Toby! The DiskStation web portal opened immediately! I am logging into our CAD projects folder!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms inbound port 5001 and secure SSL traffic are routing directly through to your NAS.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What a massive relief! My draughtsmen can resume downloading the blueprints immediately. The midnight deadline is saved.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your Hub 5 will permanently retain this public dynamic IP allocation across all future router reboots.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That will keep our DDNS service working permanently without unexpected reverts.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We also recommend setting your Synology router port forwarding rules to enforce HTTPS encryption.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: All our remote connections are forced over secure TLS 1.3.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have locked the CGNAT opt-out flag on engineering ticket NET-44019-V.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: NET-44019-V, noted down.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our Manchester gateway platform will maintain your public IP pool allocation permanently.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Toby, you understood the technical networking problem immediately.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we conclude our call, that account contact telephone number was 0161 248 8841, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, 0161 248 8841 is my office landline.

transcript.text: We have removed CGNAT carrier translation, provisioned public IP 82.132.214.88, verified Synology DDNS resolution, and confirmed remote CAD access.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Everything is working with complete perfection. Thank you Toby.
